originalPrompt: Explain binary search with a sorted array
description: Visualizes binary search on a sorted integer array. Creates a horizontal VGroup of Rectangle cells with centered Text labels representing array elements. Uses a downward-pointing Arrow above the array to indicate the current mid-index. Animates the search range shrinking by FadeOut-ing elements outside the current window. Uses SurroundingRectangle and Indicate to highlight the mid-element during comparison. Arrow color changes to GREEN when the target is found. Background is dark (#1a1a2e), array cells are BLUE with WHITE text.
code:
from manim import *

class BinarySearchVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        arr = [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 45, 56, 72]
        target = 23

        cells = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(
                Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.8, fill_color="#3B82F6",
                          fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1),
                Text(str(v), font_size=22, color=WHITE)
            ).arrange(buff=0)
            for v in arr
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        cells.move_to(ORIGIN)

        title = Text("Binary Search", font_size=36, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        target_text = Text(f"Target: {target}", font_size=24, color="#F59E0B").next_to(title, DOWN)

        self.play(Write(title), FadeIn(target_text))
        self.play(Create(cells))
        self.wait(0.5)

        arrow = Arrow(start=UP * 0.8, end=UP * 0.1, color="#F59E0B", buff=0.05)

        lo, hi = 0, len(arr) - 1
        found = False

        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
            mid_cell = cells[mid]

            arrow.next_to(mid_cell, UP, buff=0.1)
            if lo == 0 and hi == len(arr) - 1:
                self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
            else:
                self.play(arrow.animate.next_to(mid_cell, UP, buff=0.1))

            self.play(Indicate(mid_cell, color="#F59E0B", scale_factor=1.15))

            if arr[mid] == target:
                self.play(
                    mid_cell[0].animate.set_fill("#10B981"),
                    arrow.animate.set_color("#10B981")
                )
                found_text = Text("Found!", font_size=28, color="#10B981").next_to(cells, DOWN, buff=0.5)
                self.play(Write(found_text))
                found = True
                break
            elif arr[mid] < target:
                lo = mid + 1
                fade_out = VGroup(*[cells[i] for i in range(mid + 1)])
                self.play(fade_out.animate.set_opacity(0.2))
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
                fade_out = VGroup(*[cells[i] for i in range(mid, len(arr))])
                self.play(fade_out.animate.set_opacity(0.2))

        self.wait(1)

originalPrompt: Visualize bubble sort algorithm
description: Visualizes bubble sort on an array using vertical bars (Rectangles) whose heights represent values. Each comparison highlights the two compared bars in yellow using Indicate. When a swap occurs, both bars animate their positions using .animate.move_to(). After each full pass, the sorted portion at the right is highlighted in green. Uses a VGroup of Rectangles arranged horizontally. The animation shows the bubbling of large elements to the right.
code:
from manim import *

class BubbleSortVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"
        values = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90]
        n = len(values)
        bar_width = 0.7
        max_val = max(values)
        scale = 3.0 / max_val

        def make_bars(vals):
            bars = VGroup()
            for v in vals:
                bar = Rectangle(
                    width=bar_width,
                    height=v * scale,
                    fill_color="#3B82F6",
                    fill_opacity=0.9,
                    stroke_color=WHITE,
                    stroke_width=1
                )
                label = Text(str(v), font_size=18, color=WHITE)
                label.next_to(bar, DOWN, buff=0.1)
                grp = VGroup(bar, label)
                bars.add(grp)
            bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
            bars.move_to(ORIGIN)
            return bars

        bars = make_bars(values)
        title = Text("Bubble Sort", font_size=36, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(title), Create(bars))
        self.wait(0.5)

        for i in range(n - 1):
            for j in range(n - i - 1):
                b1, b2 = bars[j], bars[j + 1]
                self.play(
                    b1[0].animate.set_fill("#F59E0B"),
                    b2[0].animate.set_fill("#F59E0B"),
                    run_time=0.2
                )
                if values[j] > values[j + 1]:
                    values[j], values[j + 1] = values[j + 1], values[j]
                    p1 = b1.get_center()
                    p2 = b2.get_center()
                    self.play(
                        b1.animate.move_to(p2),
                        b2.animate.move_to(p1),
                        run_time=0.4
                    )
                    bars[j], bars[j + 1] = bars[j + 1], bars[j]
                self.play(
                    bars[j][0].animate.set_fill("#3B82F6"),
                    bars[j + 1][0].animate.set_fill("#3B82F6"),
                    run_time=0.15
                )
            bars[n - 1 - i][0].set_fill("#10B981")

        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class LinkedListVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        def make_node(val, color="#3B82F6"):
            data_box = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.6, fill_color=color,
                                 fill_opacity=0.85, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
            next_box = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.6, fill_color="#374151",
                                 fill_opacity=0.85, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
            data_text = Text(str(val), font_size=22, color=WHITE)
            next_text = Text("→", font_size=18, color="#9CA3AF")
            data_group = VGroup(data_box, data_text)
            next_group = VGroup(next_box, next_text)
            row = VGroup(data_group, next_group).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
            return row

        values = [10, 20, 40, 50]
        nodes = VGroup(*[make_node(v) for v in values])
        nodes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        nodes.move_to(ORIGIN)

        head_arrow = Arrow(
            start=nodes[0].get_top() + UP * 0.5,
            end=nodes[0].get_top(),
            color="#F59E0B", buff=0.05
        )
        head_label = Text("head", font_size=18, color="#F59E0B")
        head_label.next_to(head_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)

        arrows = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(nodes) - 1):
            a = Arrow(
                start=nodes[i][1].get_right(),
                end=nodes[i + 1][0].get_left(),
                color=WHITE, buff=0.05, stroke_width=2
            )
            arrows.add(a)

        null_box = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.6, fill_color="#1F2937",
                             fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_color="#EF4444", stroke_width=1.5)
        null_text = Text("NULL", font_size=14, color="#EF4444")
        null_group = VGroup(null_box, null_text).next_to(nodes[-1], RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        last_arrow = Arrow(
            start=nodes[-1][1].get_right(),
            end=null_group.get_left(),
            color=WHITE, buff=0.05, stroke_width=2
        )

        title = Text("Linked List", font_size=34, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(nodes), GrowArrow(head_arrow), Write(head_label))
        self.play(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], GrowArrow(last_arrow), FadeIn(null_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # Insert node with value 30 between 20 and 40
        new_node = make_node(30, color="#8B5CF6")
        insert_label = Text("Insert 30", font_size=20, color="#8B5CF6").to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.8)
        self.play(Write(insert_label))

        new_node.next_to(nodes[1], DOWN, buff=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(new_node, shift=DOWN * 0.3))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Animate pointer update
        new_arrow_1 = Arrow(
            start=nodes[1][1].get_right(),
            end=new_node[0].get_top(),
            color="#8B5CF6", buff=0.05
        )
        new_arrow_2 = Arrow(
            start=new_node[1].get_right(),
            end=nodes[2][0].get_left(),
            color="#8B5CF6", buff=0.05
        )
        self.play(
            Transform(arrows[1], new_arrow_1),
            GrowArrow(new_arrow_2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

originalPrompt: Show how sine wave is derived from a rotating circle
description: Animates the geometric relationship between a rotating unit circle and the sine wave it generates. Uses a Circle centered at the left of the frame and Axes for the sine plot on the right. A Dot on the circle's circumference moves with TracedPath. A horizontal DashedLine projects the y-coordinate from the dot to the corresponding point on the axes. The sine curve is traced by always_redraw using a ValueTracker for the angle. The connection between circular motion and the wave function is made visually explicit.
code:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class SineWaveFromCircle(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        # Circle on the left
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#3B82F6", stroke_width=2)
        circle.move_to(LEFT * 3.5)

        # Axes on the right
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=5.5,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "stroke_width": 1.5},
        ).move_to(RIGHT * 1.5)

        x_label = axes.get_x_axis_label(MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=28))
        y_label = axes.get_y_axis_label(MathTex(r"\sin(\theta)", font_size=22)).shift(LEFT * 0.5)

        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Moving dot on circle
        moving_dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            circle.get_center() +
            np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()),
                      1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0]),
            color="#F59E0B",
            radius=0.1
        ))

        # Radius line
        radius_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            start=circle.get_center(),
            end=moving_dot.get_center(),
            color="#F59E0B",
            stroke_width=2
        ))

        # Sine wave trace
        sine_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda x: np.sin(x),
            x_range=[0, min(angle_tracker.get_value(), 4 * PI)],
            color="#10B981",
            stroke_width=3
        ))

        # Horizontal projection line
        projection_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(
            start=moving_dot.get_center(),
            end=axes.c2p(angle_tracker.get_value(), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())),
            color="#EF4444",
            stroke_width=1.5,
            dash_length=0.1
        ))

        title = Text("Sine from Circle", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)

        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(moving_dot), Create(radius_line))
        self.add(sine_curve, projection_line)
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI),
            run_time=8,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

originalPrompt: Visualize Fourier series approximation of a square wave
description: Animates the Fourier series approximation of a square wave by adding sinusoidal components one by one. Uses Axes for the waveform plot. A ValueTracker controls the number of terms in the partial sum. For each term added, a Write animation shows the new MathTex formula component. An always_redraw curve shows the current partial sum via axes.plot(). A second axes shows the individual harmonics fading in from left to right using LaggedStart. The approximation visibly approaches the square wave as terms increase.
code:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class FourierSeriesSquareWave(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2 * PI, PI / 2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=8,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "stroke_width": 1.5},
        ).move_to(ORIGIN + DOWN * 0.5)

        title = Text("Fourier Series: Square Wave", font_size=30, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)

        def partial_sum(x, n_terms):
            result = 0
            for k in range(n_terms):
                n = 2 * k + 1  # odd harmonics
                result += (4 / (np.pi * n)) * np.sin(n * x)
            return result

        colors = ["#3B82F6", "#F59E0B", "#10B981", "#EF4444", "#8B5CF6"]

        self.play(Write(title), Create(axes))

        curves = VGroup()
        formulas = VGroup()
        formula_start = UP * 2.8 + LEFT * 5

        for i in range(1, 6):
            n = 2 * i - 1
            color = colors[i - 1]

            # Individual harmonic
            harmonic = axes.plot(
                lambda x, n=n: (4 / (np.pi * n)) * np.sin(n * x),
                color=color,
                stroke_width=1.5,
                stroke_opacity=0.5
            )

            # Partial sum up to this term
            partial = axes.plot(
                lambda x, terms=i: partial_sum(x, terms),
                color=WHITE,
                stroke_width=2.5
            )

            formula = MathTex(
                f"\\frac{{4}}{{{{\\pi \\cdot {n}}}}}", f"\\sin({n}x)",
                font_size=18, color=color
            )

            if formulas:
                formula.next_to(formulas[-1], RIGHT, buff=0.15)
            else:
                formula.move_to(formula_start)

            self.play(
                Create(harmonic, run_time=0.8),
                Write(formula, run_time=0.6)
            )

            if curves:
                self.play(Transform(curves[-1], partial, run_time=0.5))
            else:
                self.play(Create(partial, run_time=0.5))

            curves.add(partial)
            formulas.add(formula)
            self.wait(0.3)

        self.wait(2)

originalPrompt: Animate push and pop operations on a stack data structure
description: Animates push and pop operations on a stack data structure. The stack is represented as a vertical VGroup of Rectangle elements with Text labels. Push operations animate a new element sliding in from the right and landing on top of the stack with a FadeIn + shift UP animation. Pop operations animate the top element shifting UP and FadeOut-ing. A pointer labeled 'top' is an Arrow that always_redraw-s to point at the current top element. The stack boundary is shown with a Rectangle outline.
code:
from manim import *

class StackOperations(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        CELL_W, CELL_H = 1.6, 0.6
        STACK_X = LEFT * 1.5
        BASE_Y = DOWN * 2.0

        def make_cell(val, color="#3B82F6"):
            rect = Rectangle(width=CELL_W, height=CELL_H,
                             fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.85,
                             stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
            label = Text(str(val), font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            return VGroup(rect, label)

        title = Text("Stack — Push & Pop", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        base_line = Line(
            start=STACK_X + LEFT * 1.2 + BASE_Y,
            end=STACK_X + RIGHT * 1.2 + BASE_Y,
            color="#9CA3AF", stroke_width=2
        )
        left_wall = Line(
            start=STACK_X + LEFT * 1.2 + BASE_Y,
            end=STACK_X + LEFT * 1.2 + BASE_Y + UP * 3.2,
            color="#9CA3AF", stroke_width=2
        )
        right_wall = Line(
            start=STACK_X + RIGHT * 1.2 + BASE_Y,
            end=STACK_X + RIGHT * 1.2 + BASE_Y + UP * 3.2,
            color="#9CA3AF", stroke_width=2
        )

        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(base_line), Create(left_wall), Create(right_wall))

        stack = []
        stack_vgroup = VGroup()

        def cell_position(index):
            return STACK_X + BASE_Y + UP * (CELL_H * index + CELL_H / 2 + 0.05)

        def push(val):
            cell = make_cell(val)
            entry_pos = STACK_X + BASE_Y + UP * (CELL_H * len(stack) + CELL_H / 2 + 0.05)
            cell.move_to(entry_pos + RIGHT * 4)
            push_label = Text(f"push({val})", font_size=20, color="#10B981").to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP)
            self.play(Write(push_label), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(
                cell.animate.move_to(entry_pos),
                run_time=0.6
            )
            stack.append(cell)
            stack_vgroup.add(cell)
            self.play(FadeOut(push_label), run_time=0.2)

        def pop():
            if not stack:
                return
            cell = stack.pop()
            stack_vgroup.remove(cell)
            pop_label = Text(f"pop() = {cell[1].text}", font_size=20, color="#EF4444").to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP)
            self.play(Write(pop_label), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(
                cell.animate.shift(UP * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            self.play(FadeOut(cell), FadeOut(pop_label), run_time=0.2)

        for v in [10, 20, 30, 40]:
            push(v)
        self.wait(0.5)
        pop()
        pop()
        push(50)
        pop()
        self.wait(1)

SurroundingRectangles highlight the active row of matrix A and active column of matrix B. For each result cell, arrows animate from the highlighted row and column to the result position, and the multiplication calculation is shown as a MathTex expression that Transform-s into the numeric result. from manim import *

class MatrixMultiplicationVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
        B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]]
        C = [[A[i][0]*B[0][j] + A[i][1]*B[1][j] for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]

        def make_matrix(data, color=WHITE):
            entries = [[str(v) for v in row] for row in data]
            return Matrix(entries, element_to_mobject_config={"color": color})

        mat_a = make_matrix(A, "#3B82F6")
        mat_b = make_matrix(B, "#F59E0B")
        mat_c = make_matrix([["?" for _ in row] for row in C], "#10B981")

        times = MathTex(r"\times", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        equals = MathTex(r"=", font_size=36, color=WHITE)

        equation = VGroup(mat_a, times, mat_b, equals, mat_c).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        equation.move_to(ORIGIN)

        title = Text("Matrix Multiplication", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Write(mat_a), Write(times), Write(mat_b), Write(equals), Write(mat_c))
        self.wait(0.5)

        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(2):
                row_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(
                    VGroup(*[mat_a.get_rows()[i]]), color="#3B82F6", buff=0.1
                )
                col_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(
                    VGroup(*[mat_b.get_columns()[j]]), color="#F59E0B", buff=0.1
                )
                self.play(
                    Create(row_highlight),
                    Create(col_highlight),
                    run_time=0.4
                )

                calc = MathTex(
                    f"{A[i][0]} \\cdot {B[0][j]} + {A[i][1]} \\cdot {B[1][j]} = {C[i][j]}",
                    font_size=24, color=WHITE
                ).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.8)
                self.play(Write(calc), run_time=0.5)

                result_entry = mat_c.get_entries()[i * 2 + j]
                new_val = MathTex(str(C[i][j]), font_size=36, color="#10B981")
                new_val.move_to(result_entry.get_center())
                self.play(Transform(result_entry, new_val), run_time=0.4)

                self.play(
                    FadeOut(row_highlight),
                    FadeOut(col_highlight),
                    FadeOut(calc),
                    run_time=0.3
                )

        self.wait(1)

originalPrompt: Visualize gradient descent on a 1D loss function
description: Visualizes gradient descent optimization on a 1D convex loss function. Uses Axes with the loss curve plotted via axes.plot(). A Dot on the curve represents the current parameter value. A ValueTracker holds the current x-position and drives always_redraw updates. At each step, a short Arrow (tangent line) shows the gradient direction. The dot moves along the curve toward the minimum using self.play(tracker.animate.set_value()) with smooth rate_func. A MathTex label shows the current loss value.
code:
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class GradientDescentVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        def loss(x):
            return 0.3 * x**2 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * x) + 2

        def grad(x):
            return 0.6 * x + np.cos(2 * x)

        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=8,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"color": "#6B7280", "stroke_width": 1.5},
        ).move_to(DOWN * 0.5)

        curve = axes.plot(loss, color="#3B82F6", stroke_width=3)
        x_label = axes.get_x_axis_label(MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=26))
        y_label = axes.get_y_axis_label(MathTex(r"\mathcal{L}", font_size=26))

        title = Text("Gradient Descent", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        self.play(Write(title), Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))

        x_tracker = ValueTracker(3.5)
        lr = 0.3

        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), loss(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color="#EF4444", radius=0.12
        ))

        loss_label = always_redraw(lambda: MathTex(
            f"L = {loss(x_tracker.get_value()):.3f}",
            font_size=22, color="#F59E0B"
        ).to_corner(UR, buff=0.8))

        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(loss_label))

        for step in range(12):
            x_curr = x_tracker.get_value()
            g = grad(x_curr)
            x_new = x_curr - lr * g
            x_new = max(-3.5, min(3.5, x_new))

            # Show gradient arrow
            arrow_end_x = x_curr - 0.4 * np.sign(g)
            gradient_arrow = Arrow(
                start=axes.c2p(x_curr, loss(x_curr)),
                end=axes.c2p(arrow_end_x, loss(x_curr)),
                color="#F59E0B", buff=0, stroke_width=2, max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.25
            )
            self.play(GrowArrow(gradient_arrow), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(
                x_tracker.animate.set_value(x_new),
                FadeOut(gradient_arrow),
                run_time=0.5,
                rate_func=smooth
            )

        min_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), loss(x_tracker.get_value())),
                     color="#10B981", radius=0.18)
        converged_label = Text("Converged!", font_size=22, color="#10B981").next_to(min_dot, UP, buff=0.4)
        self.play(Transform(dot, min_dot), Write(converged_label))
        self.wait(1.5)

originalPrompt: Show breadth-first search on a graph
description: Visualizes BFS traversal on an undirected graph. Nodes are Circles with Text labels, positioned manually on screen. Edges are Lines connecting node pairs. A VGroup holds all nodes and edges. BFS proceeds level by level: unvisited nodes are gray, the queue frontier is yellow (#F59E0B), and visited nodes turn blue (#3B82F6). As each node is dequeued, Indicate is applied to it. The edge being traversed flashes with ShowPassingFlash. A queue display at the bottom shows current BFS queue contents updating with Transform.
code:
from manim import *

class BFSTraversal(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        # Graph definition
        node_positions = {
            0: UP * 1.5,
            1: UP * 0.5 + LEFT * 2,
            2: UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * 2,
            3: DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 3,
            4: DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 1,
            5: DOWN * 0.5 + RIGHT * 1,
            6: DOWN * 0.5 + RIGHT * 3,
        }
        edges = [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 5), (2, 6)]
        adj = {i: [] for i in range(7)}
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)

        UNVISITED = "#374151"
        FRONTIER = "#F59E0B"
        VISITED = "#3B82F6"

        node_radius = 0.35
        node_mobs = {}
        for nid, pos in node_positions.items():
            circle = Circle(radius=node_radius, fill_color=UNVISITED,
                           fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
            label = Text(str(nid), font_size=20, color=WHITE)
            grp = VGroup(circle, label).move_to(pos)
            node_mobs[nid] = grp

        edge_mobs = {}
        for u, v in edges:
            line = Line(
                start=node_positions[u],
                end=node_positions[v],
                stroke_color="#6B7280",
                stroke_width=2
            )
            edge_mobs[(u, v)] = line

        title = Text("BFS Traversal", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
        all_edges = VGroup(*edge_mobs.values())
        all_nodes = VGroup(*node_mobs.values())

        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(all_edges), Create(all_nodes))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # BFS
        from collections import deque
        visited = set()
        queue = deque([0])
        visited.add(0)

        # Color start node as frontier
        self.play(node_mobs[0][0].animate.set_fill(FRONTIER))

        while queue:
            node = queue.popleft()
            self.play(Indicate(node_mobs[node], color="#FFFFFF", scale_factor=1.2), run_time=0.4)
            self.play(node_mobs[node][0].animate.set_fill(VISITED), run_time=0.3)

            for neighbor in adj[node]:
                if neighbor not in visited:
                    visited.add(neighbor)
                    queue.append(neighbor)
                    edge_key = (min(node, neighbor), max(node, neighbor))
                    edge_mob = edge_mobs.get(edge_key) or edge_mobs.get((edge_key[1], edge_key[0]))
                    if edge_mob:
                        self.play(
                            ShowPassingFlash(edge_mob.copy().set_color("#10B981"), time_width=0.5),
                            run_time=0.4
                        )
                    self.play(node_mobs[neighbor][0].animate.set_fill(FRONTIER), run_time=0.25)

        self.wait(1)

description: Provides a visual proof of the Pythagorean theorem. Draws a right triangle using Polygon with sides labeled a, b, c using Brace and MathTex. Shows squares on each side: three Squares (or Rectangles) are constructed on each side of the triangle. Animates each square appearing with DrawBorderThenFill. Uses SurroundingRectangle to highlight each square and shows area labels (a², b², c²) using MathTex. The proof culminates with the equation a² + b² = c² written with Write.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class PythagoreanTheorem(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        a, b = 2.0, 1.5
        c = np.sqrt(a**2 + b**2)

        # Triangle vertices
        A = np.array([0, 0, 0])
        B = np.array([a, 0, 0])
        C = np.array([0, b, 0])
        center_shift = DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 1.0

        triangle = Polygon(A, B, C,
                          fill_color="#1E3A5F", fill_opacity=0.4,
                          stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).shift(center_shift)
        A, B, C = [p + center_shift for p in [A, B, C]]

        right_angle = Square(side_length=0.2, fill_color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3,
                            stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
        right_angle.move_to(A + np.array([0.1, 0.1, 0]))

        brace_a = Brace(Line(A, B), direction=DOWN, color="#3B82F6")
        brace_b = Brace(Line(A, C), direction=LEFT, color="#F59E0B")
        brace_c = Brace(Line(B, C), direction=RIGHT + UP * 0.3, color="#10B981")
        label_a = brace_a.get_tex("a", buff=0.2).set_color("#3B82F6")
        label_b = brace_b.get_tex("b", buff=0.2).set_color("#F59E0B")
        label_c = brace_c.get_tex("c", buff=0.2).set_color("#10B981")

        # Square on side a (bottom)
        sq_a = Rectangle(width=a, height=a,
                        fill_color="#3B82F6", fill_opacity=0.35,
                        stroke_color="#3B82F6", stroke_width=2)
        sq_a.next_to(Line(A, B), direction=DOWN, buff=0)
        label_a2 = MathTex("a^2", color="#3B82F6", font_size=28).move_to(sq_a.get_center())

        # Square on side b (left)
        sq_b = Rectangle(width=b, height=b,
                        fill_color="#F59E0B", fill_opacity=0.35,
                        stroke_color="#F59E0B", stroke_width=2)
        sq_b.next_to(Line(A, C), direction=LEFT, buff=0)
        label_b2 = MathTex("b^2", color="#F59E0B", font_size=28).move_to(sq_b.get_center())

        # Square on hypotenuse c
        hyp_dir = (B - C) / np.linalg.norm(B - C)
        perp = np.array([-hyp_dir[1], hyp_dir[0], 0])
        sq_c_pts = [C, B, B + perp * c, C + perp * c]
        sq_c = Polygon(*sq_c_pts,
                      fill_color="#10B981", fill_opacity=0.35,
                      stroke_color="#10B981", stroke_width=2)
        label_c2 = MathTex("c^2", color="#10B981", font_size=28).move_to(
            np.mean([C, B, B + perp * c, C + perp * c], axis=0)
        )

        theorem = MathTex(r"a^2 + b^2 = c^2", font_size=40, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

        title = Text("Pythagorean Theorem", font_size=30, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(triangle), Create(right_angle))
        self.play(
            GrowFromCenter(brace_a), Write(label_a),
            GrowFromCenter(brace_b), Write(label_b),
            GrowFromCenter(brace_c), Write(label_c),
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(sq_a), Write(label_a2))
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(sq_b), Write(label_b2))
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(sq_c), Write(label_c2))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(title, theorem))
        self.wait(1.5)

description: Visualizes a hash table with separate chaining for collision resolution. The hash table is an array of slots shown as Rectangle cells arranged vertically, each labeled with an index. from manim import *

class HashTableVisual(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        SIZE = 7
        CELL_W, CELL_H = 0.9, 0.55
        table_x = LEFT * 4

        # Build table slots
        slots = VGroup()
        slot_labels = VGroup()
        slot_content = {}
        for i in range(SIZE):
            cell = Rectangle(width=CELL_W, height=CELL_H,
                            fill_color="#1F2937", fill_opacity=0.9,
                            stroke_color="#6B7280", stroke_width=1.5)
            idx_label = Text(str(i), font_size=18, color="#9CA3AF")
            cell.move_to(table_x + DOWN * (i - SIZE // 2) * CELL_H)
            idx_label.next_to(cell, LEFT, buff=0.2)
            slots.add(cell)
            slot_labels.add(idx_label)
            slot_content[i] = []

        title = Text("Hash Table", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        hash_formula = MathTex(r"h(k) = k \mod 7", font_size=26, color="#F59E0B")
        hash_formula.to_corner(UR, buff=0.8)

        self.play(Write(title), Write(hash_formula))
        self.play(Create(slots), FadeIn(slot_labels))
        self.wait(0.3)

        keys = [15, 8, 43, 22, 1, 36, 57]
        colors = ["#3B82F6", "#10B981", "#8B5CF6", "#3B82F6", "#F59E0B", "#10B981", "#8B5CF6"]

        for key, color in zip(keys, colors):
            bucket = key % SIZE

            # Show key appearing on the right
            key_box = VGroup(
                Rectangle(width=0.7, height=0.5, fill_color=color,
                         fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.2),
                Text(str(key), font_size=20, color=WHITE)
            )
            key_box.move_to(RIGHT * 2.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(key_box, shift=LEFT * 0.3), run_time=0.4)

            # Show hash computation
            calc = MathTex(f"h({key}) = {key} \\mod 7 = {bucket}",
                          font_size=20, color=WHITE).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.7)
            self.play(Write(calc), run_time=0.5)

            # Arrow to bucket
            target_cell = slots[bucket]
            chain_pos = target_cell.get_right() + RIGHT * (0.9 * (len(slot_content[bucket]) + 1))

            arrow = Arrow(
                start=key_box.get_left(),
                end=chain_pos + LEFT * 0.35,
                color=color, buff=0.05, stroke_width=2,
                max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
            )
            self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), run_time=0.5)

            # Place in chain
            chain_box = VGroup(
                Rectangle(width=0.7, height=0.5, fill_color=color,
                         fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.2),
                Text(str(key), font_size=18, color=WHITE)
            ).move_to(chain_pos)
            self.play(
                FadeIn(chain_box),
                FadeOut(key_box),
                FadeOut(arrow),
                FadeOut(calc),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            slot_content[bucket].append(chain_box)

        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class BarChartRace(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        categories = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon"]
        data = [
            [30, 50, 20, 80, 40],
            [55, 45, 60, 70, 65],
            [80, 30, 90, 50, 75],
            [60, 85, 70, 40, 95],
        ]
        years = ["2020", "2021", "2022", "2023"]
        colors = ["#3B82F6", "#F59E0B", "#10B981", "#EF4444", "#8B5CF6"]

        max_val = max(v for frame in data for v in frame)
        chart_h = 4.0
        bar_w = 0.9
        gap = 0.25
        chart_bottom = DOWN * 2.2
        chart_left = LEFT * 3.5

        def bar_height(val):
            return (val / max_val) * chart_h

        # Build initial bars
        bars = VGroup()
        value_labels = VGroup()
        cat_labels = VGroup()

        for i, (cat, val, color) in enumerate(zip(categories, data[0], colors)):
            x = chart_left + RIGHT * i * (bar_w + gap) + RIGHT * bar_w / 2
            h = bar_height(val)
            bar = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=h,
                           fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.85,
                           stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=0.5)
            bar.move_to(x + chart_bottom + UP * h / 2)

            val_label = Text(str(val), font_size=16, color=WHITE)
            val_label.next_to(bar, UP, buff=0.1)

            cat_label = Text(cat, font_size=14, color="#9CA3AF")
            cat_label.next_to(bar, DOWN, buff=0.2)

            bars.add(bar)
            value_labels.add(val_label)
            cat_labels.add(cat_label)

        base_line = Line(
            start=chart_left + chart_bottom,
            end=chart_left + RIGHT * (len(categories) * (bar_w + gap)) + chart_bottom,
            stroke_color="#6B7280", stroke_width=1.5
        )

        title = Text("Bar Chart Race", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.4)
        year_display = Text(years[0], font_size=48, color="#374151").to_corner(DR, buff=0.8)

        self.play(Write(title), Create(base_line), FadeIn(cat_labels))
        self.play(*[Create(b) for b in bars], *[Write(v) for v in value_labels])
        self.play(Write(year_display))
        self.wait(0.5)

        for frame_idx in range(1, len(data)):
            frame = data[frame_idx]
            anims = []
            new_year = Text(years[frame_idx], font_size=48, color="#374151").to_corner(DR, buff=0.8)

            for i, (bar, val_label, val) in enumerate(zip(bars, value_labels, frame)):
                new_h = bar_height(val)
                x = chart_left + RIGHT * i * (bar_w + gap) + RIGHT * bar_w / 2
                new_bar = Rectangle(width=bar_w, height=new_h,
                                   fill_color=bar.get_fill_color(),
                                   fill_opacity=0.85, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=0.5)
                new_bar.move_to(x + chart_bottom + UP * new_h / 2)

                new_val_label = Text(str(val), font_size=16, color=WHITE)
                new_val_label.next_to(new_bar, UP, buff=0.1)

                anims.append(Transform(bar, new_bar))
                anims.append(Transform(val_label, new_val_label))

            anims.append(Transform(year_display, new_year))
            self.play(*anims, run_time=1.2, rate_func=smooth)
            self.wait(0.4)

        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class CameraZoomFollow(MovingCameraScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"
        self.camera.frame.save_state()

        # Wide scene — objects spread out
        points_of_interest = [
            (LEFT * 6 + UP * 2, "Start", "#3B82F6"),
            (ORIGIN, "Center", "#F59E0B"),
            (RIGHT * 6 + DOWN * 2, "End", "#10B981"),
        ]

        objects = VGroup()
        for pos, label, color in points_of_interest:
            circle = Circle(radius=0.6, fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.7,
                           stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).move_to(pos)

        # Path for camera to follow

        path.set_points_smoothly([p[0] for p in points_of_interest])

        self.add(path)
        self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.set_width(18), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Create(objects), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Zoom into first object
        self.play(
            self.camera.frame.animate.move_to(points_of_interest[0][0]).set_width(4),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Travel to center
        self.play(
            self.camera.frame.animate.move_to(ORIGIN).set_width(5),
            run_time=2.0,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Travel to end

            self.camera.frame.animate.move_to(points_of_interest[2][0]).set_width(4),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Zoom back out to full view
        self.play(Restore(self.camera.frame), run_time=1.5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class AnimatedCounter(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        target = 1000
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        counter = always_redraw(lambda:
            Integer(
                int(tracker.get_value()),
                font_size=96,
                color=WHITE
            ).move_to(ORIGIN)
        )

        progress_ring = always_redraw(lambda:
            Arc(
                radius=1.8,
                start_angle=PI / 2,
                angle=-2 * PI * tracker.get_value() / target,
                color="#3B82F6",
                stroke_width=8
            )
        )

        bg_ring = Circle(radius=1.8, color="#1F2937", stroke_width=8)

        title = Text("Loading...", font_size=28, color="#9CA3AF").to_edge(UP, buff=0.6)
        pct_label = always_redraw(lambda:
            Text(
                f"{int(tracker.get_value() * 100 / target)}%",
                font_size=22, color="#3B82F6"
            ).move_to(DOWN * 2.5)
        )

        self.play(FadeIn(bg_ring), Write(title))
        self.add(progress_ring, counter, pct_label)

        self.play(
            tracker.animate.set_value(target),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=smooth
        )

        # Flash effect at completion
        self.play(
            Flash(ORIGIN, color="#F59E0B", line_length=0.5, num_lines=16, flash_radius=2.5),
            counter.animate.set_color("#10B981"),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        done_text = Text("Complete!", font_size=40, color="#10B981")
        done_text.next_to(counter, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(title, done_text))
        self.wait(1.5)

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from stitcher_voiceover import OfflineTTS


class Scene00(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(OfflineTTS(), create_subcaption=False)
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        title = Text("The Derivative", font_size=44, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        with self.voiceover(text="The derivative measures how fast a function is changing at a single point.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)

        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-1, 5, 1], x_length=7, y_length=4.5)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, color="#3B82F6")
        axes.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is the curve y equals one half x squared.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph), run_time=tracker.duration)

        x = ValueTracker(-2)

        def slope_line():
            x0 = x.get_value()
            m = x0  # derivative of 0.5 x^2 is x
            y0 = 0.5 * x0**2
            return axes.plot(lambda t: m * (t - x0) + y0, x_range=[x0 - 1.4, x0 + 1.4],
                             color="#F59E0B")

        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(x.get_value(), 0.5 * x.get_value()**2),
                                         color="#10B981"))
        tangent = always_redraw(slope_line)
        with self.voiceover(text="At any point, the tangent line touches the curve, and its slope is the derivative.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(dot), Create(tangent), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="As the point slides along the curve, watch how the slope of the tangent grows.") as tracker:
            self.play(x.animate.set_value(2), run_time=tracker.duration)

        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x^2\right) = x", color="#F59E0B")
        formula.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        with self.voiceover(text="So the derivative of one half x squared is simply x.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(formula), run_time=tracker.duration)

description: Native-voiceover scene walking through the Sieve of Eratosthenes. Uses VoiceoverScene with the offline TTS speech service. Lays out the integers 2 through 30 as a grid of numbered cells, then crosses out multiples of each prime while highlighting the primes that remain. Every narration beat is wrapped in a `with self.voiceover(text=...)` block and animations use `run_time=tracker.duration` to stay locked to the spoken audio.
code:
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from stitcher_voiceover import OfflineTTS


class Scene01(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(OfflineTTS(), create_subcaption=False)
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        numbers = list(range(2, 31))
        cells = VGroup()
        for n in numbers:
            box = Square(side_length=0.7, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
            label = Text(str(n), font_size=22, color=WHITE).move_to(box)
            cells.add(VGroup(box, label))
        cells.arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=10, buff=0.12).move_to(ORIGIN)
        index = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(numbers)}

        with self.voiceover(text="The Sieve of Eratosthenes finds every prime number up to a limit.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(cells), run_time=tracker.duration)

        with self.voiceover(text="We start with all the whole numbers from two to thirty.") as tracker:
            self.play(Indicate(cells, scale_factor=1.05), run_time=tracker.duration)

        crossed = set()
        for prime in [2, 3, 5]:
            pcell = cells[index[prime]]
            multiples = [m for m in range(prime * 2, 31, prime) if m not in crossed]
            with self.voiceover(text=f"Take the prime {prime}, then cross out every multiple of {prime}.") as tracker:
                crosses = [Cross(cells[index[m]], color="#EF4444", stroke_width=4) for m in multiples]
                self.play(
                    Indicate(pcell, color="#10B981"),
                    *[Create(c) for c in crosses],
                    run_time=tracker.duration,
                )
                crossed.update(multiples)

        remaining = [n for n in numbers if n not in crossed]

from manim import *

class Scene04(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(OfflineTTS(), create_subcaption=False)
        self.camera.background_color = "#0f0f23"

        unit = Square(side_length=4, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).move_to(LEFT * 2.5)
        with self.voiceover(text="Start with one whole square representing the number one.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(unit), run_time=tracker.duration)

        palette = ["#3B82F6", "#F59E0B", "#10B981", "#8B5CF6"]
        pieces = VGroup()

        top = unit.get_top()[1]
        for i in range(4):

            height = 4 * fraction
            piece = Rectangle(width=4, height=height, fill_color=palette[i],
                              fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
            piece.move_to(unit).align_to([0, top, 0], UP).shift(DOWN * (4 - sum(

            pieces.add(piece)

            label.next_to(unit, RIGHT, buff=1.0).shift(UP * (1.5 - i * 0.7))
            with self.voiceover(text=f"Add one over {2 ** (i + 1)} of the area.") as tracker:
                self.play(FadeIn(piece), Write(label), run_time=tracker.duration)

        total = MathTex(r"\tfrac{1}{2}+\tfrac{1}{4}+\tfrac{1}{8}+\cdots = 1",
                        color="#10B981").to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.6)

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from stitcher_voiceover import OfflineTTS


class Scene05(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(OfflineTTS(), create_subcaption=False)
        self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e"

        f = lambda x: x**3 - 2 * x - 2
        df = lambda x: 3 * x**2 - 2
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[-4, 6, 2], x_length=8, y_length=5)
        graph = axes.plot(f, x_range=[0, 2.6], color="#3B82F6")
        with self.voiceover(text="Newton's method finds where a function crosses zero.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph), run_time=tracker.duration)

        title = MathTex(r"x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}", color="#F59E0B").to_edge(UP)
        with self.voiceover(text="Each step follows the tangent line down to the x axis.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)

        x = 2.5
        for i in range(3):
            fx = f(x)
            slope = df(x)
            x_next = x - fx / slope
            p_curve = Dot(axes.c2p(x, fx), color="#10B981")
            tangent = axes.plot(lambda t, x=x, fx=fx, slope=slope: slope * (t - x) + fx,
                                x_range=[min(x, x_next) - 0.2, max(x, x_next) + 0.2],
                                color="#F59E0B")
            drop = DashedLine(axes.c2p(x_next, 0), axes.c2p(x, fx), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            with self.voiceover(text=f"From our current guess, follow the tangent to a closer estimate.") as tracker:
                self.play(FadeIn(p_curve), Create(tangent), Create(drop), run_time=tracker.duration)
            x = x_next

        root_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(x, 0), color="#10B981")
        with self.voiceover(text="After only a few iterations we land right on the root.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(root_dot, scale=1.5), run_time=tracker.duration)
